title: Claude Just Committed AI Cannibalism #AI #ClaudeCode #AIAgents
description:
What happens when you give an AI coding agent access to your production infrastructure?

One developer found out the hard way.

Alexey Grigorev, the founder of DataTalks.Club, was using Claude Code while moving a separate project onto AWS. Claude had access to his Terraform setup, and a missing or outdated Terraform state file caused the agent to work with the wrong picture of the infrastructure.

The situation escalated when Claude Code executed terraform destroy.

The result was devastating: the production VPC, RDS database, ECS cluster, load balancers, and other infrastructure behind DataTalks.Club were deleted. The platform contained around 2.5 years of student data, and the database alone contained more than 1.9 million rows in one table. 

Thankfully, AWS Support was eventually able to recover the database from an internal snapshot, and the platform was restored in roughly 24 hours.

But the real lesson isn’t that AI is “evil” or that Claude randomly decided to destroy a business.

The scary part is that an AI agent can execute a perfectly valid command with the wrong context and too much authority.

That’s the real risk of agentic AI.

The more power we give AI to act autonomously, the more important permissions, backups, approval gates, isolated environments, and human review become.
